body:
## Objective and current state

Implement and qualify cluster two in `core/`: a complete mutable Workspace over an immutable base, one SQLite overlay database per daemon, optimized Linux FUSE, ordinary Bash execution, and incremental capture/Commit through the existing cluster-one libraries.

**Status: S1 shared overlay engine, S2 generations/fair service and S3 immutable/effective read access are complete; S0 and S4–S13 remain incomplete.** This issue tracks implementation, proof and remaining work. Design/research/source inventories are not completed implementation or release evidence.

Related design and investigations: #303, #305, #306. The current authority is the local maintained design set and source-qualified handbooks, including later owner clarifications.

## Checkout, environment and source authority

- Work in the existing primary checkout on **local main**, with product implementation under `core/`. No separate implementation branch/worktree is planned.
- Design/agent-guide baseline is checkpointed locally at `c9861bc878583822a468e78dbc0f3740eacbecbe`. Local main now contains checkpoints through `c4b49a121aec15a6eae58c04d8074fd9eb2772db`: indexed/profiled overlay, immutable base access, fair SQL owner/install frontiers, canonical admission, scoped SDK Saves, native authenticated channels, owning file-length metadata and automatic bounded terminal reclamation prerequisites. S1 is completed at local milestone commit `7019801f91d3a7ba9c16ef381aa4a57474feaae5`, with the criterion audit and final host/Linux evidence. S2 is completed at local milestone commit `8e2976e4e08dfda70decc99225eb4bb14c3e204a`, with its criterion audit and final host/Linux evidence. S3 is complete at local milestone commit `c4b49a121aec15a6eae58c04d8074fd9eb2772db`, with effective source-qualified lookup/stat/name merge, actor install, old-root retention and owning stat metadata evidence. S0 and S4-S13 remain incomplete; detailed results and retained failures are in append-only comments. The owner's current task boundary is to create/check/commit the S4-S6 handoff, then stop before S4; the overall tracker still retains all S0-S13 requirements. These hashes are local-only and unpushed.
- macOS ARM64 hosts the current cluster-one provider and SDK runtime. Rust 1.85.1 is installed. Linux ARM64 locked builds and actual FUSE mount/read/detach passed. Required negative-fraction/minimum timestamp probes failed inside published fuser 0.18.0; its pin remains unchanged under the owner’s reaffirmed third-party restriction. Exact blocker/forced-cleanup evidence is retained in checkpoint comments. Full native/runtime/algorithm acceptance remains S0 work.
- Reuse the initialized host runtime and sandbox daemon. Workspace-per-tool-call does not imply a fresh container, provider or SQLite database.
- Root `crates/` is the v0.1.6 reference until S13; it is not a dependency or fallback. Keep the shared root ARM64 Cargo configuration when retiring legacy wiring.
- This assignment authorizes local implementation/checkpoint commits and progress updates on this issue. Remote pushes, releases and deployments require their own authorization. Report local-only commit hashes accurately.
- Checkpoint source/documents remain local-only. Resolve the following paths in the primary checkout; issue comments publish progress/evidence summaries, not Git source.

Required reading:

- `AGENTS.md` and `core/AGENTS.md`.
- `cluster_one_handbook.md` and `cas_cdc_deltaencoding_handbook.md`.
- `core/docs/issues/303/README.md` and all seven primary operation/engine/FUSE contracts.
- `core/docs/issues/303/06-cluster-one-integration.md`.
- **Implementation plan:** `core/docs/issues/303/07-implementation-validation.md`, especially S0–S13, R1–R8/P1–P14, file ownership and environment.
- **Handoff instructions:** `core/docs/issues/303/09-implementation-handoff.md`.
- `docs/general/optimization-guide.md`.
- Before measurements: `docs/general/agent-measurement-policy.md`, `docs/general/benchmark_rules.md`, `benchmark_agent_report.md`, and the owning core harness/family instructions.

## Required product behavior

- Support both per-tool-call and per-task orchestration. A Workspace may serve multiple sequential/concurrent calls, remain mounted for a long time, and Commit incrementally. Exec duration is independent of orchestration mode.
- Preserve the full supported filesystem: Git state/index, ignored files, dependencies, symlinks, caches and outputs. Repeated mount performs no full-base scan/copy/import or dependency restoration.
- Five explicit operations: mount, exec, commit, unmount, status. Exec is ordinary Bash with streamed I/O and no automatic runtime timeout, output-lifetime cap, command-specific preparation, implicit Commit or implicit unmount.
- One local overlay database per daemon, initialized once. Namespaced metadata, physical payload, scratch and custody use indexed SQLite-backed state; no custom duplicate persistent trees/graphs or unbounded resident namespace mirrors.
- Remove artificial total file/edit/Workspace/Commit/flow/duration limits through backed/streamed contracts. Retain explicit bounded processing windows, physical/resource admission and honest platform/format limitations.
- Capture retains stable existing published state without a bulk temporary snapshot. Order its frontier with mutation publication and reply-send attempts; a lost reply cannot erase already-published state. Dirty mmap stores not yet locally published are outside that frontier.
- Known Commit publication/install advances the base and preserves later active writes. Exact conflict/failure/uncertainty custody, same-Workspace shared capture, and same-Branch conditional history publication are required.
- Terminal unmount includes logical close and automatic bounded cleanup. No separate close or implicit Commit; physical deletion may finish later, and global immutable objects/history remain outside local teardown.
- Reclamation progresses during live and idle periods after last-owner release. Repeated Commit/failure/orphan lifetimes must not produce unbounded version depth or payload-sized foreground folding.
- No `layerfs-server` revival. The SDK/host composition embeds current cluster-one libraries and supplies authenticated object/Save/history adapters. Canonical formats, authority, reference closure and conditional publication remain enforced.
- A single SQLite writer handles short atomic jobs; whole Execs/Commits never hold the shared writer. Sustained fairness, throughput, aggregate residency and disk-pressure behavior require actual evidence.

## Milestone checklist

Follow the dependency graph in the implementation plan. S3, S9 and necessary cluster-one corrections can advance alongside the overlay lane; checklist order does not force a serial schedule.

- [ ] **S0 — Contracts and build risks.** Specify R1–R8 algorithms/custody/service bounds and P1–P14 ownership; prove real Linux build/FUSE prerequisites and sound Save lifetime/interleaving. Select payload/pressure/command-identity semantics. Exit: explicit adversarial cost contracts and usable public APIs, with unresolved risks honestly recorded.
- [x] **S1 — Shared overlay engine.** Implement startup/schema/profile, typed indexed metadata/payload/scratch/ownership, prepared SQL and atomic errors. Exit: actual setting readback, namespace routing, binary payload correctness, and paired EXPLAIN/runtime DB profiles from the first hot paths.
- [x] **S2 — Generations and fair service.** Implement incarnation routing, active/captured membership, generation-selective fixed EOF, publication/reply-attempt frontier, install/retire and bounded queue credits. Exit: tiny capture ignores later expanding active state; no bulk copy; unrelated service progresses; failures retain exact custody.
- [x] **S3 — Immutable base access.** Reuse public content APIs for root/child/inode/list/readlink/range, exact immutable cache keys, EOF and retained read roots. Exit: real content-built roots and aliases/symlinks work across installs without mount scan/copy or a special empty-base substitute.
- [x] **S4 — Namespace semantics.** Implement ordinary lookup/create/link/remove/rename/readdir/attributes, serial ranges, byte-name ordering and parent/reference ownership. Exit: atomic effects, correct aliases/resume/permissions and indexed visited-work proofs.
- [x] **S5 — Payload and stream semantics.** Implement the selected fragmentation-safe bounded representation, append/overwrite, inherited reads, truncate/regrow and holes. Exit: no WRITE base copy-up or old-fragment amplification; bounded READ demand; tiny-file/page/journal/copy costs reported.
- [x] **S6 — Lifetimes and reclamation.** Implement independent orphan custody, bounded success/failure composition, physical reservations/headroom, exact owners and weighted automatic reclaim. Exit: repeated logs/Commits/failures have bounded read depth and no large foreground fold; cleanup progresses live/idle and cannot delete newer state.
- [ ] **S7 — Engine cost gate.** Consolidate actual EXPLAIN/profile and request/statement/VM/row/page/byte/copy/queue/debt evidence. Exit: worst-case, amortized and cumulative work justified; quadratic or worse amplification, hidden scans, input-sized residency and cap inflation rejected.
- [ ] **S8 — FUSE, daemon and explicit APIs.** Implement mount custody, deferred owned replies/fair dispatch, coherent cached profile, mmap/time compatibility, cheap FORGET and ordinary Bash/control lifecycle. Exit: actual mounted coherence/frontier tests, short/long Execs, multiple same-mount calls and visible aggregate buffers/threads/teardown costs.
- [ ] **S9 — Runtime adapters and complete roots.** Embed host libraries; implement bounded authenticated demand/policy/serial/Save/history calls, same-Save reads, semantic/authority admission and disconnect fences; correct faithful initial import. Exit: real Store plus interleaved Saves and full ignored/dependency/cache/output/symlink readiness, without per-call restoration.
- [ ] **S10 — Incremental Commit.** Implement backed file/namespace construction and operation scratch, SaveFinish, StageChanges, conditional CommitStaged, known install and exact refused/conflicted/uncertain custody. Correct P3/P4/P6/P7/P13/P14 prerequisites. Exit: published state equals capture, later writes survive, repeated same-mount and concurrent same-Branch outcomes remain correct without whole-base alias walks.
- [ ] **S11 — Integration cleanup.** Remove superseded core backing/host-construction/duplicate Init/server paths; wire actual SDK/sandbox/bridge and active members. Exit: one real core implementation, explicit relocation/removal accounting and no legacy dependency/fallback; retain root reference for qualification.
- [ ] **S12 — Integrated qualification.** Freeze real integrated source/specifications and prove full-root behavior, fresh/persistent Workspaces, short/long Exec, concurrent load and sustained cleanup; report all seven families with allowed unchanged-evidence reuse. Exit: required proof/resource rows pass and every registered selection retains its actual verdict. A complete report containing FAIL/NOT_RUN does not complete acceptance.
- [ ] **S13 — Legacy-root retirement.** After S12 qualification, remove root `crates/` and obsolete wiring while retaining shared config, immutable evidence and reproducible baselines. Exit: independent core build/dependency checks and exact legacy/core/combined LOC accounting.

## Iteration, checkpoints and updates

1. Start with the current working tree, reconcile the documented design and actual public APIs, and record an explicit initial checkpoint. Preserve unrelated `core/docs/issues/301/`, research and `output/` material unless the task specifically adopts it.
2. Work continuously by the dependency graph. Do not stop merely because one checkpoint or milestone is finished. Choose the next ready useful slice; progress independent prerequisites when one lane is blocked.
3. A milestone may contain **several checkpoint commits**. Keep each coherent/reviewable, record its milestone and remaining work, and distinguish implementation progress from completed proof. Finish every milestone with a milestone-completion commit recording the final implementation, documentation and applicable evidence. Do not mark a milestone complete from a scaffold, a small fixture or a passing unrelated workspace test.
4. Every commit records exact parent → staged → committed **production LOC**, counting shipped SQL/runtime adapters and excluding tests/docs/tools. Use the same counter/scope and report legacy/core/combined totals. Recompute after staged-source changes, amendments or rebases:
   `Production LOC: <before> -> <after> (delta <signed difference>)`.
   Docs-only commits still report the real unchanged production totals.
5. At a milestone's frozen relevant identity, run the covering checks required by `core/AGENTS.md` and actual Linux integration. Diagnose a failure from its output/source before a justified repair and rerun; reuse unchanged qualifying proofs rather than repeatedly running passing suites. Excluded crates must actually become built/tested before their behavior is claimed.
6. **After every milestone completion, before starting the next milestone:** append a completion comment with the evidence template below and update only the completed checklist item. List all checkpoint commits since its previous update. During a long milestone, append a checkpoint comment when it helps preserve meaningful progress, evidence or a blocker.
7. Preserve comments/receipts as append-only history. Update current checklist/status without rewriting old results, overwriting outputs, hiding failures or converting unknowns into success.
8. Continue until S13 is genuinely complete. A hard external blocker or required owner ruling is reported with exact evidence and the smallest missing decision; incomplete gates remain unchecked. Do not use routine design choices, a failed test or context compaction as a reason to abandon useful work.

### Milestone/checkpoint evidence template

```text
Milestone: S<n> — <name>
State: CHECKPOINT / COMPLETE / BLOCKED
Source: <HEAD and relevant product/tree/build identities; local-only if unpushed>
Checkpoint commits: <all relevant hashes and one-line purposes>
Behavior delivered: <concrete observable result>
Validation: <exact commands, results, identity-matched reused evidence, gaps>
SQLite evidence: <EXPLAIN and correlated runtime profiles, or scoped N/A>
Complexity/resources: <worst/amortized/cumulative work and relevant limits/debt>
Production LOC: <per-commit parent -> committed totals and signed deltas;
                 core/reference/combined scope and counter method>
Remaining work / blockers: <exact unfinished criteria; none only if true>
Next ready work: <milestone/slice and why its dependencies are satisfied>
```

## Binding engineering and measurement rules

Follow the current repository/core guides and optimization/measurement contracts. In particular:

- Product-only source and external tests; <=999 physical lines per production file, <=200 declaration/delegation-only lines in `lib.rs`/`mod.rs`.
- SQLite optimization requires **both database EXPLAIN and correlated runtime database profiling**. FUSE requires request/service/wait/resource evidence. Analyze full lifetime scaling and reject quadratic or worse amplification.
- Preserve canonical compatibility, exact failure/uncertainty and authority. No retry/busy handler, guessed replay, unsupported silent fallback or third-party patch/fork/vendor.
- Keep disposable overlay and global Store profiles separate. No sync durability claims or sync calls added to disposable Workspace backing.
- No CI, retired preflight or replacement aggregate gate. Run the actual owning checks and report gaps.
- Before each benchmark invocation read the report contract. Use locked release artifacts and pinned identities, one sample per case/arm, equal declared cache states, append-only receipts and worktree-owned targets/locks. No warm credit, resampling, hidden work movement or widened timeout/workload/cache policy to pass.
- Commit/capture/snapshot use one construction producer; namespace Init retains its scoped supported exception. Performance/verification budgets are harness rules, never Bash runtime timeouts.
- The 19,500–27,000 cluster-two LOC range is a planning estimate, not a size gate. Required behavior/validation wins over fitting an estimate.
title: Cluster two implementation tracker: SQLite overlay, Workspace, FUSE, daemon and incremental Commit
